intro: A fictional archive contains a missing prototype, a handwritten schedule and several unexplained deliveries.

nodes.title: The archive mystery
nodes.observation: A prototype object was absent from an archive inventory on Monday morning.
nodes.a: The object may have been misplaced during ordinary storage work.
nodes.b: The object may have been deliberately moved for a planned public display.

nodes.title: Inventory discrepancy
nodes.observation: A handwritten count differs from the electronic inventory by one item.
nodes.a: A transcription or filing error could explain the discrepancy.
nodes.b: The count may have been updated before a planned transfer was entered digitally.

nodes.title: Delivery van
nodes.observation: A delivery van was recorded at the site on Sunday.
nodes.a: The van may have delivered storage materials unrelated to the prototype.
nodes.b: The van might have transported exhibition equipment or the prototype.

nodes.title: Handwritten note
nodes.observation: A note reads: 'Monday — move the special piece'. Its author is unknown.
nodes.a: The note could refer to reorganising a shelf or storage item.
nodes.b: The note could refer to moving the prototype for display.

nodes.title: Spare key
nodes.observation: A spare storeroom key was signed out the previous week.
nodes.a: Routine maintenance may explain access to the room.
nodes.b: Staff preparing the exhibition may have needed access.

nodes.title: Event poster
nodes.observation: A draft poster advertises an upcoming exhibition of historic prototypes.
nodes.a: The event may be unrelated to the missing object.
nodes.b: The object may have been selected for the exhibition.

nodes.title: Explore conclusion
nodes.observation: These observations alone do not establish what happened.
nodes.a: Theory A: An inventory or storage error is plausible. Confirm with a recount, access records and staff interviews.
nodes.b: Theory B: A planned exhibition transfer is plausible. Confirm with transport manifests, exhibition plans and authorisation records.
